title: Meridian workspace compatibility qualification register
description: Container for the final, product-neutral qualification (record_type: workspace-compatibility-qualification) of one workspace/repository's run through the meridian-workspace-compatibility program: discovery and rule intake (existing-project-compatibility-mode.schema.json, composing instruction-source-registry.schema.json and controlled-rule-intake.schema.json), an optional migration plan (instance-data-migration.schema.json) and an optional canonical export (instance-canonical-export.schema.json). Each entry is a scoped record: its envelope (identity, scope, origin, authority) is validated against the same scoped-record.schema.json every other operating-model contract composes with, and this schema is not a second envelope schema. The record does NOT embed any composed record: payload.workspace_connection_refs/migration_plan_ref/canonical_export_ref are CLOSED pinned references, resolved through an external boundary at the library level and checked there against the REAL evaluateExistingProjectCompatibilityMode/evaluateInstanceDataMigration/evaluateInstanceCanonicalExport — never a second, competing shape for any of the three, and never a raw imported field (raw_excerpt, normalized_text, or any secret-bearing value) persisted in this record. A workspace can be connected through MORE than one scan: payload.workspace_connection_refs is a non-empty array (minItems 1) of pinned references, one per connection scan, each independently composed against the real evaluator. Every reference pins an exact sha256 content digest of the resolved record — computeConnectionDigest for each workspace connection scan, computePlanFingerprint/computeExportDigest for the migration plan and canonical export — never a bare id/reference an independent resolver could satisfy with different content under the same label; no two entries of workspace_connection_refs may declare the same id or reference. When scope.type is "project-workspace", payload.workspace_repository_ids is a REQUIRED, non-empty, unique closed list of repository ids, checked at the library level to equal EXACTLY the set of payload.repository.id names carried by every resolved connection — no repository scanned but undeclared, no repository declared but unscanned, no repository scanned twice; when scope.type is "repository-scope" the field is forbidden, and payload.workspace_connection_refs itself is closed to AT MOST ONE entry (maxItems 1) — a repository-scope record names exactly one repository through scope.id, and a multi-repository workspace is expressed only through one project-workspace record's workspace_connection_refs, never through several repository-scope records sharing a workspace_id. payload.qualification_state is a closed, RECOMPUTED verdict — QUALIFIED, BLOCKED or UNVERIFIED — checked at the library level against the composed evaluations' own outcome aggregated across EVERY declared connection (a blocking next_step or an undecided rule candidate on ANY one of them forces the same non-QUALIFIED result as it would alone, regardless of declaration order); a declared state that does not match the recomputed one is rejected, never trusted on its own. blockers/open_questions are closed to qualification_state: blockers is non-empty exactly when BLOCKED, open_questions is non-empty exactly when UNVERIFIED. This package does not migrate, export, scan, or accept any rule; it only qualifies — declares one closed verdict over records produced by the five packages it composes. The contract is a mandatory part of the Kernel: an absent schema or absent fixtures is a validator FAIL, not an informational skip. The normative document is standards/workspace/workspace-compatibility-qualification.md.

entry.description: workspace_repository_ids is required exactly when this entry's own scope.type is "project-workspace" and forbidden otherwise (repository-scope names one repository through scope.id itself and carries no separate repository list); payload.workspace_connection_refs itself is closed to at most one entry when scope.type is "repository-scope" (one repository, one scan — a second scan of the SAME single repository is never a second legal entry, and multiple repositories are expressed only through scope.type "project-workspace", never through several repository-scope records, workspace-compatibility-qualification.md §2) — the one place this schema reads a sibling of `payload` to constrain `payload`'s own required set or array bound, mirroring scoped-record.schema.json's own scope/origin/authority cross-field allOf.

pinned_ref.description: A closed reference resolved through an external boundary — never an embedded body. sha256 is mandatory on all three uses of this shape in this schema: the exact composed version's own recomputed content digest (computeConnectionDigest/computePlanFingerprint/computeExportDigest), never a bare id/reference an independent resolver could satisfy with different content under the same label.

workspace_connection_refs.description: Always required, at least one entry: a qualification without at least one pinned, resolvable workspace connection scan does not exist. One entry per connection scan this record composes — a multi-repository project-workspace names one entry per repository it covers. Each entry's sha256 pins that resolved record's own recomputed computeConnectionDigest; no two entries may declare the same id or reference (checked at the library level, since uniqueItems alone would not catch two entries sharing an id or reference under a differing sha256).

workspace_repository_ids.description: Required exactly when this entry's scope.type is "project-workspace", forbidden otherwise (see the entry-level allOf). The closed, unique set of repository ids this record claims workspace_connection_refs covers — checked at the library level to equal EXACTLY the set of payload.repository.id names carried by every resolved connection: no repository scanned but undeclared, no repository declared but unscanned, no repository scanned twice.

migration_plan_ref.description: null when this qualification composes no migration plan; otherwise a pinned reference to one FULL instance-data-migration entry, sha256-pinned to its recomputed plan_fingerprint.

canonical_export_ref.description: null when no canonical export is composed; otherwise a pinned reference to one FULL instance-canonical-export entry, sha256-pinned to its recomputed digest. Present only meaningfully alongside a non-null migration_plan_ref.
